correctness.rationale: A facet needs at least n−1 active signed roots. All n cannot be active since the sum of an odd number of ±1 potential increments cannot be zero. The remaining increment is an even integer of absolute value at most one, hence zero. Each omitted edge and balanced sign sequence gives one simplex. Its cone from the origin is a signed path-root simplex with incidence Gram determinant n, so the facet area is sqrt(n) times the normalized normal norm divided by (n−2)!. This is intrinsic Euclidean area. A uniform actual facet gives a uniform balanced sequence; for a squared partial-sum difference spanning d of m=n−1 increments the mean is d(m−d)/(m−1), rather than d for an unconditioned path. Applying the pairwise variance identity and summing over pairs gives (n²−1)/12 for the centered cycle potential norm squared, and twice that for the path. The bridge invariance principle and uniform Riemann sums give the stated centered periodic bridge functional. The periodic Green kernel has paired sine/cosine eigenvalues (2pi k)^(−2), giving the stated Laplace law, mean, and variance. The finite squared normal moment bounds the L² norm of the scaled unsquared areas and so ensures convergence of their means. The surface ratio follows from these means and the central-binomial facet-count ratio. Exact independent Gram computations at n=3,5,7,9 covered 806 facets by cyclic symmetry; mean squares were 2, 5/18, 7/3600, 1/423360. Numerical quadrature yielded ratio coefficient 0.583488362048 at two resolutions (not a rigorous decimal certificate).
